items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: The definition should describe motion in both directions about a mean position.
rubric.description: Defines vibratory motion as repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing repeated motion in both directions about a mean or equilibrium position.

rubric.why: A correct example completes the answer.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of vibratory motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable example.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the repeated to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.
Example: the prongs of a tuning fork vibrate about their mean position.

items.followUp: A body has a weight of 98 N. Find its mass if g = 9.8 m/s².

rubric.why: The answer needs the relation between weight and mass, rearranged to find mass.
rubric.description: States and rearranges the weight–mass relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for W = mg and m = W ÷ g.

rubric.why: The given values produce a mass of 14.7 kg.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and gives the mass with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: weight, W = 147 N; gravitational acceleration, g = 10 m/s².
Formula: W = mg, so m = W ÷ g.
Answer: the mass of the body is 14.7 kg.

items.followUp: What is another name for a solar cell, and what semiconductor layers are joined to make it?

rubric.why: Photovoltaic cell is another name for a solar cell.
rubric.description: Names a solar cell as a photovoltaic cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct name.

rubric.why: A solar cell is made by joining semiconductor layers to form a P–N junction.
rubric.description: Describes the construction using joined P-type and N-type semiconductor layers, commonly silicon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the P-type and N-type layers or the P–N junction with silicon.

modelAnswer: A solar cell is also called a photovoltaic cell.
It is made by joining P-type and N-type layers of a semiconductor, usually silicon, to form a P–N junction.

items.followUp: Describe four ways of reducing friction in machines or when moving through a fluid.

rubric.why: Lubricants reduce direct rubbing between surfaces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for oil, grease, or another suitable lubricant.

rubric.why: Smoother surfaces have fewer irregularities that interlock.
rubric.description: Polishes or smooths the surfaces in contact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for polishing or otherwise smoothing the surfaces.

rubric.why: Rolling friction is less than sliding friction.
rubric.description: Uses ball bearings or rollers to replace sliding friction with rolling friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for ball bearings or rollers.

rubric.why: A streamlined shape reduces resistive friction in air or water.
rubric.description: Streamlines the shape of a body moving through a fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for streamlining or a suitable streamlined shape.

modelAnswer: Lubricate the surfaces with oil or grease to reduce rubbing.
Polish or smooth the surfaces in contact.
Use ball bearings or rollers to replace sliding friction with rolling friction.
Give bodies moving through air or water a streamlined shape to reduce fluid friction.
